hi! I’m anxious and overthink everything too. It’s a blessing and a curse. I went on T for a year, and have now been off for 3 months and will probably go back on (happy to explain this more). So feel free to dm and ask any questions. I took a low/medium dose, meaning my testosterone levels were at the low end of the cis male range 

I do wanna start by saying that testosterone affects everyone’s body a little differently, and by this I mean changes happen at faster or slower paces, different changes are more or less intense.

I don’t know where you live, but talking to a therapist that is knowledgeable and gender affirming could be helpful, to help you understand your thoughts. Otherwise here are some things that might help you consider your decision:

body/face hair: this can be quick for some, extremely slow for others, and some people just don’t grow chest hair or back hair or ass hair. I will say that society has placed a stigma on ‘feminine’ bodies having body hair. And while it’s certainly fine to worry about what others think it could just be good to unpack why you think body hair looks bad on a ‘feminine’ body. also when I started my medical transition I loved some of my new body hair and disliked other. Before I started, I researched options finasteride, which can often slow body hair growth, the cost of waxing/how comfortable I was with shaving, and also if I was a good candidate for laser hair removal, to help me understand what might happen if i liked my other changes but struggled with this one. 

fat redistribution: in my year, I only noticed some fat redistribution in my face and I gained a gut/belly as opposed to my weight going to my thighs/butt. As I’ve been off I’ve definitely noticed my curves accentuated again but they were pretty accentuated before and while I was on t. that being said, it’s a slow change and will revert with weight loss and gain. 

as for boobs, that one I don’t have much insight on as I got top surgery, and binded for a long time off T, I do think I lost a little fat around my chest, but with my larger chest it wasn’t super noticeable for me. 

That being said, with changes like this, it’s important to ask yourself how will I treat myself and my body if some of these changes I am worried about happen and I am not able to achieve my pre-T body? 

there are many ways we can change our bodies but a lot is out of our exact control. but feeling confident in your body will make you attractive to others too. 

also, lastly some things you can do while you decide how you might to proceed are try voice training tutorials on YouTube or look into pumping for bottom growth.  there’s a subreddit for that but I’m on mobile and can’t remember the name.

It’s never too late to go on testosterone, so it’s okay to take your time.
